props.title: Fury of the Dragon
props.initialSlug: Bruce Lee's lost footage brought to explosive life

sections.content: **Fury of the Dragon** (1976) represents Bruce Lee's final completed film footage, assembled posthumously following his tragic death in 1973. While often overshadowed by **Enter the Dragon** (1973) and Fist of Fury (1972), this compilation film captures Lee at his physical peak, showcasing the lightning-fast strikes and charismatic screen presence that revolutionized martial arts cinema. The film draws from Lee's earlier works, including footage from **Game of Death** (1978) and various fight sequences that influenced later kung fu classics like **The 36th Chamber of Shaolin** (1978).

sections.content: The mid-1970s marked a crucial transition in martial arts cinema. Following Lee's death, the genre split into two distinct paths: the gritty realism championed by The Street Fighter (1974) starring Sonny Chiba, and the more acrobatic wuxia style seen in **Five Deadly Venoms** (1978). **Fury of the Dragon** (1976) sits at this crossroads, incorporating both Lee's practical fighting philosophy and the theatrical elements that would define later Hong Kong action films.

The film's influence extends beyond martial arts cinema. The quick-cut editing style used to emphasize Lee's speed influenced directors like **Jackie Chan** in **Drunken Master** (1978) and later Hollywood action films like **The Bourne Identity** (2002). The practice of compiling posthumous footage would unfortunately become common in martial arts cinema, seen again with Brandon Lee in **The Crow** (1994). SUBHEAD: The Bruce Lee Legacy

sections.content: While **Fury of the Dragon** (1976) may not represent Lee's strongest work, it serves as an important historical document of his revolutionary impact on action cinema. His emphasis on realistic combat and philosophical depth influenced countless films, from **Kill Bill: Vol. 1** (2003) to **The Raid: Redemption** (2011). The film also captures the transition period in Hong Kong cinema between traditional kung fu films and the more modern action style that would emerge in the 1980s with films like **Police Story** (1985).
